1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	We systematically compare \cls{}, \cwm{}, and \traj{} across two representative code LLM families, two complexity levels, and multiple seeds to characterize the formulation design space for neural code verification.
5	
6	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
7	\label{sec:setup}
8	
9	\paragraph{Datasets.}
10	\emph{Function-level}: mutated variants from HumanEval~\cite{chen2021humaneval} and MBPP~\cite{austin2021mbpp} (five mutation types), labels verified by execution. 19,076 samples (train 15,290 / val 1,896 / test 1,890; pass:fail $\approx$ 52:48, majority baseline 51.75\%).
11	\emph{Repo-level}: per-test instances from SWE-bench Verified~\cite{chowdhury2024swebenchverified} mutants. ${\sim}$70K training samples; val ($n{=}9{,}335$) and test ($n{=}9{,}784$) have zero problem overlap (majority baseline 72.96\%). Val-based checkpoint selection follows standard practice~\cite{jimenez2024swebench} where validation loss is computable; runs using truncate preprocessing produce NaN validation loss due to length-mismatched sequences, which defaults to the final epoch checkpoint (affects DeepSeek s123 and all \cwm{} runs; see Appendix~\ref{app:hyperparams}).
12	
13	\paragraph{Models and training.}
14	We fine-tune Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B~\cite{qwen2025qwen3} with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)~\cite{hu2022lora} (rank 16, 3 epochs) across five seeds. Seeds 42/123/456 use bfloat16; seeds 789/0 use NormalFloat 4-bit (NF4) quantization~\cite{dettmers2024qlora} to test robustness to precision reduction (function-level accuracy remains within seed noise across both precisions; see footnote in \S\ref{sec:equivalence}). As a cross-model consistency check, we additionally fine-tune DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B~\cite{guo2024deepseekcoder} with identical LoRA configuration (2 seeds each for \cls{} and \cwm{}). Our \cwm{} baseline is a LoRA fine-tuned variant for matched comparison, not a reproduction of the 32B Code World Model~\cite{meta2025cwm}. Repo-level models use val-selected checkpoints where available; runs with NaN validation loss use the final epoch checkpoint (Appendix~\ref{app:hyperparams}). Zero-shot baselines use Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B (NF4) as LLM-as-judge. Full hyperparameter details appear in Appendix~\ref{app:hyperparams}.
15	
16	\paragraph{Statistics.}
17	Confidence intervals use clustered bootstrap~\cite{davison1997bootstrap} (114 problem clusters, 10K resamples; we resample entire problems, not individual tests, to preserve within-problem correlations); per-test vs.\ trajectory-level equivalence uses Two One-Sided Tests (TOST)~\cite{schuirmann1987tost} with $\pm$2 percentage point (\pp{}) margin. Holm-Bonferroni correction~\cite{holm1979} controls family-wise error rate across the four primary comparisons (Table~\ref{tab:holm}). Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)~\cite{shrout1979icc} quantifies within-problem correlation. Oracle analysis uses SWE-bench Verified (500 instances).
18	
19

21	\label{sec:func_results}
22

92	\cwm{} flat scaling ($-$0.03\pp{}) may reflect suboptimal hyperparameter transfer at 8B rather than a fundamental limitation; we do not claim generation \emph{cannot} benefit from scale. At function level, outputs are short (integers, booleans) and format compliance is near-perfect; at repo level, output length grows to ${\sim}$477 tokens on average, and the same generation bottleneck manifests as format collapse (51--74\% unparseable; \S\ref{sec:repo}). \traj{} also shows no scaling benefit at repo level (72.92\% at both 4B and 8B); only \cls{} scales positively across both complexity levels.

95	\subsection{Per-Test vs.\ Trajectory-Level Equivalence}
96	\label{sec:equivalence}
97	
98	We compare \cls{} (aggregated via all-pass rule) against \traj{} on 523 variant-level instances across five seeds.\footnote{Seeds 789 and 0 use NF4 quantized inference; the remaining three use bfloat16. Restricting to bfloat16 seeds only (3 seeds) yields $p{=}0.128$: consistent in direction but underpowered due to reduced seed coverage.} The pooled gap is $-$0.45\pp{} (95\% CI [$-$1.71, +0.84]); the TOST equivalence test confirms statistical equivalence at $p = 0.007$ ($\pm$2\pp{} margin, Holm-Bonferroni corrected). Our $\pm$2\pp{} threshold follows the SESOI framework~\cite{lakens2017}, set independently of the observed gap and grounded in deployment relevance: at function-level accuracy (85--88\%), a 2\pp{} difference corresponds to ${\sim}$38 per-test predictions across 1,890 tests (${\sim}$2--3 problems out of 114)---comparable to between-seed variation (0.37--0.97\pp{} std, Table~\ref{tab:main_results}) and checkpoint selection noise ($<$1\pp{}, \S\ref{sec:threats}). A difference within this range is indistinguishable from training noise for pipeline selection decisions. Equivalence holds at margins as tight as $\pm$1.52\pp{} (Table~\ref{tab:tost_sensitivity}), well below the pre-specified threshold. Within-problem predictions are correlated (intraclass correlation ICC $= 0.191$, $p < 0.0001$, design effect (DEFF) $= 3.97$); all statistical tests use clustered bootstrap accordingly. On DeepSeek-Coder, the observed \cls{}--\cwm{} gap of 0.02\pp{} is consistent with equivalence, but with only 2 seeds the comparison is underpowered. Notably, the DeepSeek \cls{}--\traj{} gap (2.69\pp{}) exceeds the $\pm$2\pp{} margin, indicating that \traj{} parity is model-dependent rather than universal; the \cls{}--\cwm{} equivalence is robust across both families. Per-test classification provides diagnostic information (which specific tests fail) at no cost to variant-level accuracy, a result that parallels process supervision~\cite{lightman2023letsverify}, where step-level verification enables error localization without accuracy cost.

210	\subsection{Analysis}
211	\label{sec:analysis}
212	
213	\paragraph{Aggregation penalty.} Under the all-pass rule, a single false negative flips the variant verdict. The penalty ranges from 1.36\pp{} (DeepSeek s42) to 19\pp{} (Qwen3-4B), depending on fail recall and test count (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:variant_level}). Val-based checkpoint selection biases toward per-test accuracy at the expense of fail recall, which amplifies the penalty. \traj{} avoids this by predicting variant outcomes directly (72.92--75.35\%). The penalty is predictable from test count: function-level variants ($\bar{T} \approx 2.3$) incur negligible penalty, while repo-level variants ($\bar{T} \gg 10$) incur substantial penalty, both the \emph{advantage} and \emph{cost} of per-test granularity concentrate at high $T$ (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}(a)).
214	
215	\paragraph{Why does generation degrade at repo level?} Output space complexity increases nonlinearly: function-level outputs are short strings (integers, booleans); repo-level outputs are unconstrained execution traces (mean ${\sim}$477 tokens) where errors compound multiplicatively, and cause format collapse (53--74\% unparseable). Even among parseable outputs, accuracy (38--43\%) is below majority baseline, which indicates a semantic gap beyond format compliance (Appendix~\ref{app:qualitative}).
216	
217	\cls{} achieves 217$\times$ higher throughput than \cwm{} (1 output token vs.\ avg 477), consistent across both model families.
218	
219	\paragraph{Error complementarity.} At function level, \cls{} and \cwm{} exhibit partial complementarity: both are FP-dominant (over-predict failure), but at different rates (\cls{} 56.5\%, \cwm{} 70.3\%; Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}(a)), so \cwm{} over-predicts failure on instances \cls{} correctly classifies. An oracle combination achieves 90.63\% (+2.80\pp{} over the best single formulation; single-seed estimate). At repo level, oracle routing across configurations reaches 95.83\% variant accuracy (+14.58\pp{} over the best single configuration, $n{=}48$), the strongest evidence that the formulation design space contains complementary solutions worth exploring. A re-repair pilot found no benefit from per-test diagnostics ($n{=}44$, $p{=}0.42$; Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}(j)). Extended analysis appears in Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}.
220	
221	\subsection{Threats to Validity}
222	\label{sec:threats}
223	
224	We identify five potential confounds and assess their individual impact in Appendix~\ref{app:threats}: checkpoint selection (a checkpoint ablation on Qwen3-8B \cls{} s42 shows $<$1\pp{} variation: epoch~1 85.34\%, val-selected 84.48\%, final 85.29\%; \cwm{} epoch ablation shows $<$2\pp{} difference between epochs 2--3, suggesting training duration is not the primary driver of \cwm{} underperformance; NaN validation loss forces final-epoch default in all \cwm{} runs and DeepSeek s123), evaluation sequence length (${\sim}$1.5\pp{} for \cls{}), preprocessing (qualitative ranking holds; the ${\sim}$8\pp{} cross-configuration variance in DeepSeek \cls{} is predominantly preprocessing-driven), \traj{} training regime (downsample confirms formulation advantage), and \cwm{} scale/pretraining (primary limitation; all repo-level \cwm{} conclusions conditional on the ${\leq}$8B LoRA regime). The 19--26\pp{} gap exceeds any single assessed confound, but the combination of limited seeds and correlated confounds means definitive causal attribution requires the multi-seed replication currently underway. Holm-Bonferroni correction confirms the two core claims survive (adjusted $p{=}0.012$ and $p{=}0.021$; Table~\ref{tab:holm}).

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

We systematically compare \cls{}, \cwm{}, and \traj{} across two representative code LLM families, two complexity levels, and multiple seeds to characterize the formulation design space for neural code verification.

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:setup}

\paragraph{Datasets.}
\emph{Function-level}: mutated variants from HumanEval~\cite{chen2021humaneval} and MBPP~\cite{austin2021mbpp} (five mutation types), labels verified by execution. 19,076 samples (train 15,290 / val 1,896 / test 1,890; pass:fail $\approx$ 52:48, majority baseline 51.75\%).
\emph{Repo-level}: per-test instances from SWE-bench Verified~\cite{chowdhury2024swebenchverified} mutants. ${\sim}$70K training samples; val ($n{=}9{,}335$) and test ($n{=}9{,}784$) have zero problem overlap (majority baseline 72.96\%). Val-based checkpoint selection follows standard practice~\cite{jimenez2024swebench} where validation loss is computable; runs using truncate preprocessing produce NaN validation loss due to length-mismatched sequences, which defaults to the final epoch checkpoint (affects DeepSeek s123 and all \cwm{} runs; see Appendix~\ref{app:hyperparams}).

\paragraph{Models and training.}
We fine-tune Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B~\cite{qwen2025qwen3} with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)~\cite{hu2022lora} (rank 16, 3 epochs) across five seeds. Seeds 42/123/456 use bfloat16; seeds 789/0 use NormalFloat 4-bit (NF4) quantization~\cite{dettmers2024qlora} to test robustness to precision reduction (function-level accuracy remains within seed noise across both precisions; see footnote in \S\ref{sec:equivalence}). As a cross-model consistency check, we additionally fine-tune DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B~\cite{guo2024deepseekcoder} with identical LoRA configuration (2 seeds each for \cls{} and \cwm{}). Our \cwm{} baseline is a LoRA fine-tuned variant for matched comparison, not a reproduction of the 32B Code World Model~\cite{meta2025cwm}. Repo-level models use val-selected checkpoints where available; runs with NaN validation loss use the final epoch checkpoint (Appendix~\ref{app:hyperparams}). Zero-shot baselines use Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B (NF4) as LLM-as-judge. Full hyperparameter details appear in Appendix~\ref{app:hyperparams}.

\paragraph{Statistics.}
Confidence intervals use clustered bootstrap~\cite{davison1997bootstrap} (114 problem clusters, 10K resamples; we resample entire problems, not individual tests, to preserve within-problem correlations); per-test vs.\ trajectory-level equivalence uses Two One-Sided Tests (TOST)~\cite{schuirmann1987tost} with $\pm$2 percentage point (\pp{}) margin. \subsection{Per-Test vs.\ Trajectory-Level Equivalence}
\label{sec:equivalence}

We compare \cls{} (aggregated via all-pass rule) against \traj{} on 523 variant-level instances across five seeds.\footnote{Seeds 789 and 0 use NF4 quantized inference; the remaining three use bfloat16. Restricting to bfloat16 seeds only (3 seeds) yields $p{=}0.128$: consistent in direction but underpowered due to reduced seed coverage.} The pooled gap is $-$0.45\pp{} (95\% CI [$-$1.71, +0.84]); the TOST equivalence test confirms statistical equivalence at $p = 0.007$ ($\pm$2\pp{} margin, Holm-Bonferroni corrected). Our $\pm$2\pp{} threshold follows the SESOI framework~\cite{lakens2017}, set independently of the observed gap and grounded in deployment relevance: at function-level accuracy (85--88\%), a 2\pp{} difference corresponds to ${\sim}$38 per-test predictions across 1,890 tests (${\sim}$2--3 problems out of 114)---comparable to between-seed variation (0.37--0.97\pp{} std, Table~\ref{tab:main_results}) and checkpoint selection noise ($<$1\pp{}, \S\ref{sec:threats}). A difference within this range is indistinguishable from training noise for pipeline selection decisions. Equivalence holds at margins as tight as $\pm$1.52\pp{} (Table~\ref{tab:tost_sensitivity}), well below the pre-specified threshold. Within-problem predictions are correlated (intraclass correlation ICC $= 0.191$, $p < 0.0001$, design effect (DEFF) $= 3.97$); all statistical tests use clustered bootstrap accordingly. On DeepSeek-Coder, the observed \cls{}--\cwm{} gap of 0.02\pp{} is consistent with equivalence, but with only 2 seeds the comparison is underpowered. Notably, the DeepSeek \cls{}--\traj{} gap (2.69\pp{}) exceeds the $\pm$2\pp{} margin, indicating that \traj{} parity is model-dependent rather than universal; the \cls{}--\cwm{} equivalence is robust across both families. Per-test classification provides diagnostic information (which specific tests fail) at no cost to variant-level accuracy, a result that parallels process supervision~\cite{lightman2023letsverify}, where step-level verification enables error localization without accuracy cost.

Oracle analysis on SWE-bench Verified (500 instances) shows that per-test advantage concentrates at $T \geq 2$ fail-to-pass tests (31.3\% of instances, contributing 55.3\% of the total oracle advantage; Appendix~\ref{app:oracle}).

\subsection{Analysis}
\label{sec:analysis}

\paragraph{Aggregation penalty.} Under the all-pass rule, a single false negative flips the variant verdict. The penalty ranges from 1.36\pp{} (DeepSeek s42) to 19\pp{} (Qwen3-4B), depending on fail recall and test count (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:variant_level}). Val-based checkpoint selection biases toward per-test accuracy at the expense of fail recall, which amplifies the penalty. \traj{} avoids this by predicting variant outcomes directly (72.92--75.35\%). The penalty is predictable from test count: function-level variants ($\bar{T} \approx 2.3$) incur negligible penalty, while repo-level variants ($\bar{T} \gg 10$) incur substantial penalty, both the \emph{advantage} and \emph{cost} of per-test granularity concentrate at high $T$ (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}(a)).

\paragraph{Why does generation degrade at repo level?} Output space complexity increases nonlinearly: function-level outputs are short strings (integers, booleans); repo-level outputs are unconstrained execution traces (mean ${\sim}$477 tokens) where errors compound multiplicatively, and cause format collapse (53--74\% unparseable). Even among parseable outputs, accuracy (38--43\%) is below majority baseline, which indicates a semantic gap beyond format compliance (Appendix~\ref{app:qualitative}).

\cls{} achieves 217$\times$ higher throughput than \cwm{} (1 output token vs.\ avg 477), consistent across both model families.

\paragraph{Error complementarity.} At function level, \cls{} and \cwm{} exhibit partial complementarity: both are FP-dominant (over-predict failure), but at different rates (\cls{} 56.5\%, \cwm{} 70.3\%; Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}(a)), so \cwm{} over-predicts failure on instances \cls{} correctly classifies. An oracle combination achieves 90.63\% (+2.80\pp{} over the best single formulation; single-seed estimate). At repo level, oracle routing across configurations reaches 95.83\% variant accuracy (+14.58\pp{} over the best single configuration, $n{=}48$), the strongest evidence that the formulation design space contains complementary solutions worth exploring. A re-repair pilot found no benefit from per-test diagnostics ($n{=}44$, $p{=}0.42$; Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}(j)). Extended analysis appears in Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}.

\subsection{Threats to Validity}
\label{sec:threats}

We identify five potential confounds and assess their individual impact in Appendix~\ref{app:threats}: checkpoint selection (a checkpoint ablation on Qwen3-8B \cls{} s42 shows $<$1\pp{} variation: epoch~1 85.34\%, val-selected 84.48\%, final 85.29\%; \cwm{} epoch ablation shows $<$2\pp{} difference between epochs 2--3, suggesting training duration is not the primary driver of \cwm{} underperformance; NaN validation loss forces final-epoch default in all \cwm{} runs and DeepSeek s123), evaluation sequence length (${\sim}$1.5\pp{} for \cls{}), preprocessing (qualitative ranking holds; the ${\sim}$8\pp{} cross-configuration variance in DeepSeek \cls{} is predominantly preprocessing-driven), \traj{} training regime (downsample confirms formulation advantage), and \cwm{} scale/pretraining (primary limitation; all repo-level \cwm{} conclusions conditional on the ${\leq}$8B LoRA regime). The 19--26\pp{} gap exceeds any single assessed confound, but the combination of limited seeds and correlated confounds means definitive causal attribution requires the multi-seed replication currently underway. Holm-Bonferroni correction confirms the two core claims survive (adjusted $p{=}0.012$ and $p{=}0.021$; Table~\ref{tab:holm}).

19	# 论文写作风格规范

25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证

34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**

38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机

42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用

91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
209	- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	### 6.5 页面节奏
214	
215	好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：
216	
217	- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
218	- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
219	- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
220	- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
221	- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）
222	
223	### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范
224	
225	**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
226	- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
227	- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
228	- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
229	- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
230	- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）
231	
232	**宽度决策树**：
233	- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
234	- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
235	- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix
236	
237	---
238	
239	## 七、投稿前通用准备
240	
241	### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）
242	
243	- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
244	- **不要用**：
245	  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
246	  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
247	  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
248	- 风险：
249	  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
250	  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
251	  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
252	- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
253	- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致
254	
255	### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对
256	
257	- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
258	- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
259	- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
260	- 行号开启（review 版常需）
261	- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件
262	
263	### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程
264	
265	提交前必须逐一检查：
266	1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
267	2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
268	3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
269	4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
270	5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
271	6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
272	7. 所有专有名词有定义
273	8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
274	9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
275	10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

### 3.2 整体叙事结构

```
现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念

---

### 4.3 禁忌

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

---

## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）

- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash

  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```

- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句

- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用

1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）

## 六、图表与视觉规范

### 6.1 知识密度原则

- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure

### 6.2 表格规范

- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
- 小数精度全表统一
- 最优加粗、次优下划线
- Caption 必须自包含

### 6.3 图片规范

- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页

### 6.4 空间效率

- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比

### 6.5 页面节奏

好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：

- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）

### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范

**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）

**宽度决策树**：
- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix

---

## 七、投稿前通用准备

### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）

- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
- **不要用**：
  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
- 风险：
  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致

### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对

- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
- 行号开启（review 版常需）
- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件

### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程

提交前必须逐一检查：
1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
7. 所有专有名词有定义
8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础

\section{Experiments}
\label{sec:experiments}

We systematically compare \cls{}, \cwm{}, and \traj{} across two representative code LLM families, two complexity levels, and multiple seeds to characterize the formulation design space for neural code verification.

\subsection{Experimental Setup}
\label{sec:setup}

\paragraph{Datasets.}
\emph{Function-level}: mutated variants from HumanEval~\cite{chen2021humaneval} and MBPP~\cite{austin2021mbpp} (five mutation types), labels verified by execution. 19,076 samples (train 15,290 / val 1,896 / test 1,890; pass:fail $\approx$ 52:48, majority baseline 51.75\%).
\emph{Repo-level}: per-test instances from SWE-bench Verified~\cite{chowdhury2024swebenchverified} mutants. ${\sim}$70K training samples; val ($n{=}9{,}335$) and test ($n{=}9{,}784$) have zero problem overlap (majority baseline 72.96\%). Val-based checkpoint selection follows standard practice~\cite{jimenez2024swebench} where validation loss is computable; runs using truncate preprocessing produce NaN validation loss due to length-mismatched sequences, which defaults to the final epoch checkpoint (affects DeepSeek s123 and all \cwm{} runs; see Appendix~\ref{app:hyperparams}).

\paragraph{Models and training.}
We fine-tune Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B~\cite{qwen2025qwen3} with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA)~\cite{hu2022lora} (rank 16, 3 epochs) across five seeds. Seeds 42/123/456 use bfloat16; seeds 789/0 use NormalFloat 4-bit (NF4) quantization~\cite{dettmers2024qlora} to test robustness to precision reduction (function-level accuracy remains within seed noise across both precisions; see footnote in \S\ref{sec:equivalence}). As a cross-model consistency check, we additionally fine-tune DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B~\cite{guo2024deepseekcoder} with identical LoRA configuration (2 seeds each for \cls{} and \cwm{}). Our \cwm{} baseline is a LoRA fine-tuned variant for matched comparison, not a reproduction of the 32B Code World Model~\cite{meta2025cwm}. Repo-level models use val-selected checkpoints where available; runs with NaN validation loss use the final epoch checkpoint (Appendix~\ref{app:hyperparams}). Zero-shot baselines use Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B (NF4) as LLM-as-judge. Full hyperparameter details appear in Appendix~\ref{app:hyperparams}.

\paragraph{Statistics.}
Confidence intervals use clustered bootstrap~\cite{davison1997bootstrap} (114 problem clusters, 10K resamples; we resample entire problems, not individual tests, to preserve within-problem correlations); per-test vs.\ trajectory-level equivalence uses Two One-Sided Tests (TOST)~\cite{schuirmann1987tost} with $\pm$2 percentage point (\pp{}) margin. Holm-Bonferroni correction~\cite{holm1979} controls family-wise error rate across the four primary comparisons (Table~\ref{tab:holm}). Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)~\cite{shrout1979icc} quantifies within-problem correlation. Oracle analysis uses SWE-bench Verified (500 instances).


\subsection{Function-Level Results}
\label{sec:func_results}

Table~\ref{tab:main_results} reports function-level results across formulations and model families.

\label{tab:main_results}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
\begin{tabular}{llcc}

All three formulations achieve comparable accuracy on Qwen3-4B: \cls{} 88.43\% ($\pm$0.78), \cwm{} 87.19\% ($\pm$0.37), \traj{} 86.30\% ($\pm$0.97). DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B shows: \cls{} 86.85\%, \cwm{} 86.83\%, \traj{} 84.16\%. The \cls{}--\cwm{} gap (0.02--1.24\pp{}) is within seed noise in both families. However, the \cls{}--\traj{} gap is model-dependent: $<$1\pp{} on Qwen3 but 2.69\pp{} on DeepSeek-Coder, exceeding the $\pm$2\pp{} equivalence margin (\S\ref{sec:equivalence}). \cls{} and \cwm{} are robustly equivalent; \traj{} parity is model-contingent. Zero-shot baselines (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}) establish that repo-level verification requires fine-tuning (0-shot$\to$fine-tuned gains of 25--35\pp{}) and that formulation choice matters only at repo level (\cls{} outperforms \cwm{} by 13--26\pp{}).


\subsection{Scaling Behavior}
\label{sec:scaling}

Table~\ref{tab:scaling} compares all three formulations at two model sizes using seeds 42 and 123, both trained in full bfloat16 precision (excluding NF4 seeds to isolate the size effect).

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Model-size scaling: accuracy (\%) at 4B and 8B (Qwen3, seeds 42/123, full bfloat16 precision). \cls{} and \traj{} scale positively; \cwm{} does not.}
\label{tab:scaling}
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
\begin{tabular}{llcccc}
\toprule

\midrule

\cls{} & 8B & \textbf{90.48} & 89.40 & \textbf{89.94} & \\
\midrule
\cwm{} & 4B & 87.51 & 87.20 & 87.36 & \multirow{2}{*}{$-$0.03} \\
\cwm{} & 8B & 87.67 & 86.98 & 87.33 & \\
\midrule
\traj{} & 4B & 85.27 & 86.72 & 86.00 & \multirow{2}{*}{+1.70} \\
\traj{} & 8B & 87.60 & 87.79 & \underline{87.70} & \\

\end{table}

\cls{} and \traj{} both scale positively from 4B to 8B (+1.27\pp{} and +1.70\pp{} respectively), while \cwm{} remains flat ($-$0.03\pp{}). At 8B, the ranking is \cls{} (89.94) $>$ \traj{} (87.70) $>$ \cwm{} (87.33). The \cls{}--\cwm{} gap widens from 1.32\pp{} at 4B to 2.62\pp{} at 8B (Figure~\ref{fig:scaling_gap}); clustered bootstrap on the 3-seed superset (42, 123, 456 for \cls{}/\cwm{}) yields $p = 0.0066$ (95\% CI $[1.80, 2.71]$), which confirms the widening is not a sampling artifact.

\cwm{} flat scaling ($-$0.03\pp{}) may reflect suboptimal hyperparameter transfer at 8B rather than a fundamental limitation; we do not claim generation \emph{cannot} benefit from scale. At function level, outputs are short (integers, booleans) and format compliance is near-perfect; at repo level, output length grows to ${\sim}$477 tokens on average, and the same generation bottleneck manifests as format collapse (51--74\% unparseable; \S\ref{sec:repo}). \traj{} also shows no scaling benefit at repo level (72.92\% at both 4B and 8B); only \cls{} scales positively across both complexity levels.


\subsection{Per-Test vs.\ Trajectory-Level Equivalence}
\label{sec:equivalence}

We compare \cls{} (aggregated via all-pass rule) against \traj{} on 523 variant-level instances across five seeds.\footnote{Seeds 789 and 0 use NF4 quantized inference; the remaining three use bfloat16. Restricting to bfloat16 seeds only (3 seeds) yields $p{=}0.128$: consistent in direction but underpowered due to reduced seed coverage.} The pooled gap is $-$0.45\pp{} (95\% CI [$-$1.71, +0.84]); the TOST equivalence test confirms statistical equivalence at $p = 0.007$ ($\pm$2\pp{} margin, Holm-Bonferroni corrected). Our $\pm$2\pp{} threshold follows the SESOI framework~\cite{lakens2017}, set independently of the observed gap and grounded in deployment relevance: at function-level accuracy (85--88\%), a 2\pp{} difference corresponds to ${\sim}$38 per-test predictions across 1,890 tests (${\sim}$2--3 problems out of 114)---comparable to between-seed variation (0.37--0.97\pp{} std, Table~\ref{tab:main_results}) and checkpoint selection noise ($<$1\pp{}, \S\ref{sec:threats}). A difference within this range is indistinguishable from training noise for pipeline selection decisions. Equivalence holds at margins as tight as $\pm$1.52\pp{} (Table~\ref{tab:tost_sensitivity}), well below the pre-specified threshold. Within-problem predictions are correlated (intraclass correlation ICC $= 0.191$, $p < 0.0001$, design effect (DEFF) $= 3.97$); all statistical tests use clustered bootstrap accordingly. On DeepSeek-Coder, the observed \cls{}--\cwm{} gap of 0.02\pp{} is consistent with equivalence, but with only 2 seeds the comparison is underpowered. Notably, the DeepSeek \cls{}--\traj{} gap (2.69\pp{}) exceeds the $\pm$2\pp{} margin, indicating that \traj{} parity is model-dependent rather than universal; the \cls{}--\cwm{} equivalence is robust across both families. Per-test classification provides diagnostic information (which specific tests fail) at no cost to variant-level accuracy, a result that parallels process supervision~\cite{lightman2023letsverify}, where step-level verification enables error localization without accuracy cost.

Oracle analysis on SWE-bench Verified (500 instances) shows that per-test advantage concentrates at $T \geq 2$ fail-to-pass tests (31.3\% of instances, contributing 55.3\% of the total oracle advantage; Appendix~\ref{app:oracle}).


\subsection{Repo-Level: Preliminary Evidence for Complexity-Dependent Divergence}
\label{sec:repo}

Checkpoints are val-selected where validation loss is computable (\S\ref{sec:setup}); the test set has zero problem overlap with validation.

\subsection{Analysis}
\label{sec:analysis}

\paragraph{Aggregation penalty.} Under the all-pass rule, a single false negative flips the variant verdict. The penalty ranges from 1.36\pp{} (DeepSeek s42) to 19\pp{} (Qwen3-4B), depending on fail recall and test count (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:variant_level}). Val-based checkpoint selection biases toward per-test accuracy at the expense of fail recall, which amplifies the penalty. \traj{} avoids this by predicting variant outcomes directly (72.92--75.35\%). The penalty is predictable from test count: function-level variants ($\bar{T} \approx 2.3$) incur negligible penalty, while repo-level variants ($\bar{T} \gg 10$) incur substantial penalty, both the \emph{advantage} and \emph{cost} of per-test granularity concentrate at high $T$ (Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}(a)).

\paragraph{Why does generation degrade at repo level?} Output space complexity increases nonlinearly: function-level outputs are short strings (integers, booleans); repo-level outputs are unconstrained execution traces (mean ${\sim}$477 tokens) where errors compound multiplicatively, and cause format collapse (53--74\% unparseable). Even among parseable outputs, accuracy (38--43\%) is below majority baseline, which indicates a semantic gap beyond format compliance (Appendix~\ref{app:qualitative}).

\cls{} achieves 217$\times$ higher throughput than \cwm{} (1 output token vs.\ avg 477), consistent across both model families.

\paragraph{Error complementarity.} At function level, \cls{} and \cwm{} exhibit partial complementarity: both are FP-dominant (over-predict failure), but at different rates (\cls{} 56.5\%, \cwm{} 70.3\%; Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}(a)), so \cwm{} over-predicts failure on instances \cls{} correctly classifies. An oracle combination achieves 90.63\% (+2.80\pp{} over the best single formulation; single-seed estimate). At repo level, oracle routing across configurations reaches 95.83\% variant accuracy (+14.58\pp{} over the best single configuration, $n{=}48$), the strongest evidence that the formulation design space contains complementary solutions worth exploring. A re-repair pilot found no benefit from per-test diagnostics ($n{=}44$, $p{=}0.42$; Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}(j)). Extended analysis appears in Appendix~\ref{app:extended_analysis}.

\subsection{Threats to Validity}
\label{sec:threats}

We identify five potential confounds and assess their individual impact in Appendix~\ref{app:threats}: checkpoint selection (a checkpoint ablation on Qwen3-8B \cls{} s42 shows $<$1\pp{} variation: epoch~1 85.34\%, val-selected 84.48\%, final 85.29\%; \cwm{} epoch ablation shows $<$2\pp{} difference between epochs 2--3, suggesting training duration is not the primary driver of \cwm{} underperformance; NaN validation loss forces final-epoch default in all \cwm{} runs and DeepSeek s123), evaluation sequence length (${\sim}$1.5\pp{} for \cls{}), preprocessing (qualitative ranking holds; the ${\sim}$8\pp{} cross-configuration variance in DeepSeek \cls{} is predominantly preprocessing-driven), \traj{} training regime (downsample confirms formulation advantage), and \cwm{} scale/pretraining (primary limitation; all repo-level \cwm{} conclusions conditional on the ${\leq}$8B LoRA regime). The 19--26\pp{} gap exceeds any single assessed confound, but the combination of limited seeds and correlated confounds means definitive causal attribution requires the multi-seed replication currently underway. Holm-Bonferroni correction confirms the two core claims survive (adjusted $p{=}0.012$ and $p{=}0.021$; Table~\ref{tab:holm}).
